chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ عِمْرَانُ الْحَلَبِيُّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: And ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ رَجُلٍ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَبِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ وَقَدْ تَمَتَّعَ ثُمَّ عَجَّلَ فَقَبَّلَ امْرَأَتَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقَصِّرَ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ

translations.en: about a man who circumambulated the House and went between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah while performing tamattuʿ, then hastened and kissed his wife before trimming from his head.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ دَمٌ يُهَرِيقُهُ وَإِنْ جَامَعَ فَعَلَيْهِ جَزُورٌ أَوْ بَقَرَةٌ».

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "He must offer sacrificial blood which he sheds; and if he had intercourse, then upon him is a camel or a cow."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the mutamattiʿ who engages in intimacy before trimming the hair and thereby before fully exiting ihram. Kissing the wife entails a sacrificial penalty, while intercourse entails a heavier expiation of a camel or a cow.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone performing tamattuʿ who kisses or has intercourse with his wife before trimming his hair?

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two hills of saʿy
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other hill of saʿy
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to trim the hair as part of release from ihram
key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial animal offering due as expiation
